Summary: US-01: Customer opening the self-service portal session
Description:
h3. User story

As a customer that's routed to self-service, I want to open a portal session, so that I can view and act on my account without calling an agent

h3. Business value

Enables the ~40% self-service scope claimed for OPP-02

h3. Acceptance criteria

Session starts only if the eligibility routing confirms self-service and the session has a unique reference linked to the account. Lastly, idle sessions trigger the abandonment exception.

h3. Dependencies 

US-10 (Eligibility Routing)

Summary: US-02: Verify customer identity using SMS/email
Description:
h3. Story

As a customer, I want to verify my identity using a one-time code sent by SMS or email, so that my account information stays protected.

h3. Business value

Required precondition for OPP-02 and linked to Daniel's audit/compliance concern.

h3. Acceptance criteria

The code is single-use and time-limited; account/balance data is hidden until verification succeeds; verification result is logged with a timestamp.

h3. Dependencies

US-01

Summary: US-03: Confirm the existing authorisation system integration for identity verification
Description:
h3. Story

As the delivery team, we want confirmation of whether SMS/email verification integrates with an existing customer authentication system or needs a new build, so that estimation and design are accurate.

h3. Business value

Prevents a late-discovered integration blocker on the critical path to OPP-02.

h3. Acceptance criteria

IT/Security confirms integration approach in writing; outcome is documented before US-02 development starts; no code is written against an unconfirmed assumption.

h3. Dependencies

None

h3. Story

As the Portal System, I want to consolidate legacy DB, spreadsheet, and email records into a single unified customer record, so that every downstream feature reads consistent, trustworthy data.

h3. Business value

OPP-01 — highest-ranked, positive base-case ROI opportunity, it also de-risks all other Phase 1 stories.

h3. Acceptance criteria

The record includes balance, history, and status from all three sources; conflicting values resolve per the agreed governance rule (e.g., legacy DB wins); record updates automatically whenever a portal or agent action occurs.

h3. Dependencies

US-05

Summary: US-05: Agree on data governance and conflict resolution rules
Description:
h3. Story

As Operations and Finance, we want an agreed rule for which data source wins when the legacy DB, spreadsheet, and email disagree, so that the unified record is trustworthy from day one.

h3. Business value

Precondition for US-04; addresses SN-037's "scattered systems" pain point properly rather than superficially.

h3. Acceptance criteria

a single documented rule set exists and is signed off by Operations and Finance; the rule is testable (i.e., a QA tester can verify a conflict resolves as documented).

h3. Dependencies

None

h3. Story

As a verified customer, I want to see my balance, due date, and payment history, so that I understand what I owe without calling an agent.

h3. Business value

Directly answers SN-001 and SN-002.

h3. Acceptance criteria

The summary reflects the unified record in real time; a fallback message appears if data is temporarily unavailable rather than showing blank/incorrect figures; communication history is visible and read-only.

h3. Dependencies

US-02 and US-04

Summary: US-07: Present the available self-service actions
Description:
h3. Story

As a verified customer, I want to choose between making a manual payment or capturing a promise to pay, so that I can resolve my case in the way that suits me.

h3. Business value

Core self-service decision point supporting OPP-02's time-savings case.

h3. Acceptance criteria

Only manual payment and promise-to-pay options are offered, therefore no payment-plan selection option is shown (out of scope); an idle timeout on this screen triggers abandonment logging (US-12).

h3. Dependencies

US-06

h3. Story

As a customer, I want to make a one-off manual payment through the portal, so that I can resolve my balance without agent involvement.

h3. Business value

Directly reduces agent call volume (part of OPP-02's 8–14 min/case saved).

h3. Acceptance criteria

Payment amount and method are validated before submission; a confirmation is shown on success; a failed payment routes the customer back to the action screen (US-07), not to a dead end.

h3. Dependencies

US-07

h3. Story

As a customer, I want to submit a promised payment date and amount, so that I can confirm my commitment without an agent call.

h3. Business value

Addresses SN-045/SN-112; the capture-only half of OPP-05 that Gareth specifically asked for.

h3. Acceptance criteria

Promised date must be in the future; promised amount must be greater than zero; no automated escalation timer is triggered on submission (that half of OPP-05 is out of scope); confirmation is shown to the customer.

h3. Dependencies

US-07

Summary: US-10: Record the self-service outcome to the unified record and communication logs
Description:
h3. Story

As the Portal System, I want every self-service action (payment or promise) written back to the unified customer record and communication log in one call, so that agents and reporting always see the latest status.

h3. Business value

OPP-03 — positive base-case ROI; eliminates manual re-entry (SN-038).

h3. Acceptance criteria

The recording happens automatically immediately after US-08 or US-09 completes; write updates both the unified record and the audit log in a single transaction; failure to write is retried or flagged, never silently dropped.

h3. Dependencies

US-04, US-08, US-09

Summary: US-11: Route the ineligible cases to an agent
Description:
h3. Story

As the Portal System, I want to check whether an account is eligible for self-service before opening a portal session, so that unsuitable cases go straight to an agent instead of a confusing self-service journey.

h3. Business value

Protects Amina's requirement that straightforward and complex cases aren't tangled together.

h3. Acceptance criteria

An eligibility check runs immediately after the unified record is created (A2); ineligible cases are routed to the agent queue with the reason attached; the check does not apply payment-plan eligibility logic (out of scope).

h3. Dependencies

US-04

Summary: US-12: Handle the failed identity verification
Description:
h3. Story

As a customer who fails identity verification, I want a clear retry path and an eventual handoff to an agent, so that I'm not stuck with no way forward.

h3. Business value

Prevents silent drop-off on a critical-path feature (identity verification blocks all self-service).

h3. Acceptance criteria

The failed attempts are counted; up to a defined retry limit (e.g., 3) the customer can retry; beyond the limit the case routes to an agent with a note that self-service verification failed.

h3. Dependencies

US-02

Summary: US-13: Detect and log the customer abandonment
Description:
h3. Story

As the Portal System Manager, I want to detect when a customer leaves a session idle beyond a defined threshold, so that the case can be followed up appropriately instead of silently disappearing.

h3. Business value

Prevents cases from being lost between self-service and agent-led handling; supports honest reporting on portal effectiveness.

h3. Acceptance criteria

The idle threshold (e.g., 10 minutes) is configurable; abandonment is logged with the last screen viewed; abandoned cases are flagged for optional agent follow-up, not automatically escalated.

h3. Dependencies

US-01

Summary: US-14: Agent reviews the preloaded unified profile during handoff
Description:
h3. Story

As a Collections Agent, I want the full unified customer profile pre-loaded when a case is routed to me, so that I don't need to ask the customer to repeat information already given.

h3. Business value

Directly addresses SN-037 (first-contact context); preserves agent context on every handoff type (ineligible routing, failed verification, abandonment).

h3. Acceptance criteria

The profile includes communication history, payment history, and any self-service actions already attempted; no manual lookup step exists in the agent's task; profile is identical regardless of which exception path (US-11, US-12, US-13) triggered the handoff.

h3. Dependencies

US-04, US-10

Summary: US-15: Escalate hardships, dispute and/or legal cases to specialist processes
Description:
h3. Story

As a Collections Agent, I want to escalate a case to the appropriate specialist process with full context attached, so that the specialist doesn't start from scratch.

h3. Business value

Keeps high-risk/complex cases out of automation per Amina's segmentation principle, without losing context on handoff.

h3. Acceptance criteria

The escalation sends the full unified record and escalation reason; the receiving process is referenced but not built as part of this story (out of scope); the case is marked "on hold — specialist owns" in the unified record.

h3. Dependencies

US-04, US-14

Summary: US-16: Log the agent-led outcomes automatically
Description:
h3. Story

As a Collections Agent, I want my contact outcome logged automatically to the unified record after I select it, so that I don't need to re-key it into multiple systems.

h3. Business value

OPP-03 — same positive-ROI logging mechanism as US-10, applied to the agent-led path.

h3. Acceptance criteria

The outcome codes are structured (no free text); a single save action updates the unified record and audit log; no duplicate entry is required in any other system.

h3. Dependencies

US-04, US-14

Summary: US-17: Provide real-time status visibility for operations managers
Description:
h3. Story

As an Operations Manager, I want to view live case status on demand, so that I no longer need to run a weekly manual reconciliation.

h3. Business value

Directly resolves SN-122/SN-085 (inconsistent status codes) and the "manual status reconciliation" pain point (Part 3); delivers the "clearer reporting" measurable outcome.

h3. Acceptance criteria

The dashboard reads live from the same unified record/communication log that US-10 and US-16 write to; status codes are standardized (no per-agent variation); no scheduled batch/reconciliation job is required to see current status.

h3. Dependencies

US-04, US-10, US-16
